title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: VANESSA'S SALON
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Vanessa, who owns a tiny hair salon in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.
She had not taken a single day off in eleven years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE YES LADY
segments.quote: I cannot give you the formula for success, but I can give you the formula for failure, which is: try to please everybody.
segments.author: Herbert Bayard Swope
lines: Vanessa said yes to everybody. Six a.m. haircut? Yes. Free trim for a cousin's cousin? Yes.
One night, eating cold gumbo at the front desk, she read a line from the newspaper man Herbert Bayard Swope:
I cannot give you the formula for success, but I can give you the formula for failure, which is: try to please everybody.
So she stuck a note on her mirror. One word. No.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TWO THINGS
segments.quote: To do two things at once is to do neither.
segments.author: Publilius Syrus
lines: Saying no was hard. Doing ten jobs at once was harder.
One Friday, she answered the phone while coloring Miss Odette's hair. Miss Odette went home a little bit green.
Her husband Ray, who reads old Roman books, quoted Publilius Syrus:
To do two things at once is to do neither.
So Vanessa set up online booking, and the phone stayed quiet.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE NEW STYLIST
segments.quote: Never tell people how to do things. Tell them what to do and they will surprise you with their ingenuity.
segments.author: George S. Patton
lines: Next, she hired a young stylist named Tasha. Then stood behind her all day, saying, not like that.
Ray left a note on the coffee pot, from General George Patton:
Never tell people how to do things. Tell them what to do and they will surprise you with their ingenuity.
So Vanessa stepped back. Tasha invented a braid so popular, people drove in from Lafayette.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BREAK ROOM
segments.quote: One of the symptoms of approaching nervous breakdown is the belief that one's work is terribly important.
segments.author: Bertrand Russell
lines: Still, Vanessa was tired. One afternoon, she cried in the break room.
Tasha sat down next to her, and read from the British thinker Bertrand Russell:
One of the symptoms of approaching nervous breakdown is the belief that one's work is terribly important.
Vanessa laughed so hard she snorted. Then she booked her first vacation in eleven years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BEACH
segments.quote: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Four days at Gulf Shores. On day one, she called the salon nine times. What if the shop burned down?
Ray took her phone, and quoted the Roman thinker Seneca:
We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
The phone went in the hotel safe. Vanessa went in the ocean.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: MONDAYS
segments.quote: A broad margin of leisure is as beautiful in a man's life as in a book.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: When she came back, the salon was fine. Tasha was booked for a month.
Then Vanessa found a line in the journal of Henry David Thoreau:
A broad margin of leisure is as beautiful in a man's life as in a book.
So now the salon closes on Mondays. And Vanessa goes fishing with Ray, on purpose.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say no. Do one thing. Trust people. Take the break. Stop worrying. Leave room to live.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say no sometimes. Do one thing at a time. Trust your people. Take the break. Stop worrying. And leave some room in your life.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And nobody tell me how to comb my moustache.
